plates.title: The Chronicle of the Replication Crisis
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, aged parchment tone, dense black ink linework with muted gold, ochre and faded blue washes, in the register of a medieval chronicle. The composition runs top to bottom in strict reading order, each vignette enclosed in its own round or oval frame, connected by thin inked ribbon-paths that show the argument's flow. At the very top: THE CRACKED TABLET (a scribe copying a splitting tablet) feeds down into THE MEASURING WALL (a scholar before labeled instruments). A ribbon leads to THE CHRONICLE OF ORIGINS cluster: FOUR TORCHES OF WARNING (a chronicler among four lit torches), then THE CRUMBLING PILLAR (robed scholars alarmed at a toppling pillar), then THE WEAK HOURGLASS (an old hourglass trickling weakly on a dusty shelf) — these three enclosed together in a single large framed region labeled only by their own vignette titles. Ribbons converge from this region down into an EVIDENCE ACROSS FIELDS enclosure containing four side-by-side roundels: THE FIELD OF BANNERS (ninety-seven small banners, a third upright), THE APOTHECARY'S JARS (fifty-three jars, most cracked), THE LAGGING MERCHANT (a merchant trailing a caravan with ledgers), and beneath them all converging into THE GATHERING OF FAILURES (a large central roundel of robed figures around a basin of failed flasks). From that gathering, two ribbons fork into a CAUSES enclosure split into two framed columns: left column holds THE LOCKED DRAWER (a clerk hiding gray scrolls) above THE CROOKED CROSSROADS (a gambler nudging dice at a many-pathed table); right column holds THE BENT SCALE (a judge's scale bending under a cushion). Both columns funnel down into THE QUARREL ON THE BRIDGE (two groups of robed figures shouting across a bridge), which leads to a RESPONSE enclosure containing THE NEW CORNERSTONE (masons laying a cornerstone over the ruined pillar) and finally, at the very bottom, THE THREE SIGHTING-RODS (a surveyor fixing one point from three hills). Fine marginal foliage only in the untouched corners, kept sparse so the vignettes dominate the page; no lettering anywhere except each vignette's title in small capitals directly beneath its frame.

vignettes.quote: widespread failures to reproduce published scientific results
vignettes.depicts: A scribe at the top of the page holds up a cracked tablet of results, the inscription splitting in two as it is copied by a second scribe.
vignettes.title: THE CRACKED TABLET

vignettes.quote: Certain terms commonly used in discussions of the replication crisis have technically precise meanings
vignettes.depicts: A small glossary-scene: a scholar points with a rod to a wall of carefully labeled measuring instruments (scales, hourglass, ruler).
vignettes.title: THE MEASURING WALL

vignettes.quote: Felipe Romero identified four precursors to the crisis
vignettes.depicts: A robed chronicler named Romero stands before four lit torches, each representing a separate warning fire.
vignettes.title: FOUR TORCHES OF WARNING

vignettes.quote: a "crisis of confidence" in psychology and other fields
vignettes.depicts: A council of robed scholars with their hands raised in alarm around a toppling pillar labeled nothing, just crumbling stone.
vignettes.title: THE CRUMBLING PILLAR

vignettes.quote: low power persisted for 50 years, indicating a structural and persistent problem
vignettes.depicts: An old hourglass that has run fifty turns, sand still trickling weakly, ignored on a dusty shelf.
vignettes.title: THE WEAK HOURGLASS

vignettes.quote: Of 97 original studies with significant effects, 36% replicated successfully
vignettes.depicts: A field of ninety-seven small planted banners, only about a third still standing upright, the rest fallen.
vignettes.title: THE FIELD OF BANNERS

vignettes.quote: only 11% of 53 pre-clinical cancer studies had replications that could confirm conclusions
vignettes.depicts: A row of fifty-three sealed jars on an apothecary's shelf, nearly all cracked and spilled, a handful intact.
vignettes.title: THE APOTHECARY'S JARS

vignettes.quote: Economics has lagged behind other social sciences and psychology in its attempts to assess replication rates
vignettes.depicts: A merchant with ledgers trailing behind a caravan of other scholars already far down the road.
vignettes.title: THE LAGGING MERCHANT

vignettes.quote: more than 70% of researchers have tried and failed to reproduce another scientist's experiment results
vignettes.depicts: A great gathering of robed figures, most shaking their heads over failed alchemical flasks before a central basin where all their paths converge.
vignettes.title: THE GATHERING OF FAILURES

vignettes.quote: Publication bias—the tendency to publish only positive, significant results—creates the "file drawer effect"
vignettes.depicts: A clerk stuffing plain gray scrolls into a locked drawer while only gilded scrolls go up on display.
vignettes.title: THE LOCKED DRAWER

vignettes.quote: Questionable research practices are behaviors that exploit researcher degrees of freedom
vignettes.depicts: A gambler's hand nudging dice at a crossroads table with many open paths painted on the floor.
vignettes.title: THE CROOKED CROSSROADS

vignettes.quote: null hypothesis testing is itself inappropriate, especially in "soft sciences" like social psychology
vignettes.depicts: A judge's scale shown bending oddly under a soft cushion instead of a firm weight.
vignettes.title: THE BENT SCALE

vignettes.quote: unidentified "adversaries" names such as "methodological terrorist" and "self-appointed data police"
vignettes.depicts: Two groups of robed figures shouting across a narrow bridge, one side pointing accusing fingers at the other.
vignettes.title: THE QUARREL ON THE BRIDGE

vignettes.quote: the replication crisis is a foundation for a "credibility revolution"
vignettes.depicts: Masons laying a new cornerstone over the crumbled pillar from earlier in the chronicle.
vignettes.title: THE NEW CORNERSTONE

vignettes.quote: research should emphasize triangulation, not just replication, to protect against flawed ideas
vignettes.depicts: A surveyor using three sighting-rods from different hills to fix one true point on a valley below.
vignettes.title: THE THREE SIGHTING-RODS

plates.title: The Eight Provinces of Evidence
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page continuing the same hand, aged parchment, black ink linework with muted gold, ochre and faded blue wash. The page is divided into eight small framed provincial roundels arranged in two columns down the upper two-thirds, each a distinct 'territory' of evidence, connected by thin ribbon-paths all flowing downward and inward. Left column, top to bottom: THE FIELD OF BANNERS (ninety-seven small banners planted in a field, a third upright), THE EMPTY JARS (a physician before mostly-empty apothecary jars), THE COOKBOOK'S WARNINGS (a cook with an open cookbook, scholars pinning warnings to hanging ingredients), THE SHRUNKEN WEIGHING (a merchant's scale showing a shrunken second pile of coin-sacks). Right column, top to bottom: THE VAST CROWD (a cartographer with one small compass before thousands of tiny figures), THE SHELF OF CURES (a healer with ninety-two gleaming vials), THE DRY RIVERBED (a surveyor over a vast dry riverbed with one tiny trickle marked genuine), THE SHIFTING ORACLE (a clerk puzzled before a mechanical oracle giving different answers). All eight ribbon-paths run down and converge into one large central roundel at the page's midpoint: THE GATHERING OF FAILURES, robed figures from all eight lands standing together shaking their heads around a shared basin. A single ribbon continues from this convergence down to the final roundel at the bottom of the page: THE TATTERED SCROLL, PRAISED, showing a crowd of scholars eagerly copying a torn, unreliable scroll while a sound, intact scroll lies ignored beside it — the ironic twist closing the composition. Keep margins sparse, mostly bare parchment with only faint hairline foliage in the corners, so the ten framed scenes remain large and legible. No lettering anywhere on the page except each vignette's title in small capitals beneath its own frame.

vignettes.quote: Of 97 original studies with significant effects, 36% replicated successfully
vignettes.depicts: A field of ninety-seven small planted banners, a third standing, under a banner reading nothing but shown as a bare pennant.
vignettes.title: THE FIELD OF BANNERS

vignettes.quote: the replication of such studies requires samples from thousands of individuals due to small effect sizes
vignettes.depicts: A cartographer straining to measure a vast crowd of thousands of tiny figures with one small compass.
vignettes.title: THE VAST CROWD

vignettes.quote: Results from The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology suggest most studies of the cancer research sector may not be replicable
vignettes.depicts: A physician examining a row of apothecary jars under a project banner, most jars found empty.
vignettes.title: THE EMPTY JARS

vignettes.quote: 92% found that the studied therapies were effective
vignettes.depicts: A healer presenting ninety-two gleaming vials of cure out of a near-complete set on a shelf.
vignettes.title: THE SHELF OF CURES

vignettes.quote: out of a random sample of 50 ingredients from a cookbook, 80% had articles reporting on their cancer risk
vignettes.depicts: A cook holding an open cookbook while scholars pin warning notices to most of fifty hanging ingredients.
vignettes.title: THE COOKBOOK'S WARNINGS

vignettes.quote: approximately 61% of studies successfully replicated, though the replicated effect sizes were only 66% of the original reported effect sizes
vignettes.depicts: A merchant weighing coin-sacks on a scale, the second weighing showing a visibly smaller pile than the first.
vignettes.title: THE SHRUNKEN WEIGHING

vignettes.quote: study results might be reproduced for only 0.6% to 6.8%
vignettes.depicts: A surveyor beside a vast dry riverbed map, only a tiny trickle of water marked as genuine.
vignettes.title: THE DRY RIVERBED

vignettes.quote: their outputs can shift from one run to the next even when settings are held constant
vignettes.depicts: A mechanical oracle-device giving a different answer each time the same lever is pulled by a puzzled clerk.
vignettes.title: THE SHIFTING ORACLE

vignettes.quote: more than 70% of researchers have tried and failed to reproduce another scientist's experiment results
vignettes.depicts: All eight provincial paths converging into a wide central basin where robed figures from every land stand shaking their heads together.
vignettes.title: THE GATHERING OF FAILURES

vignettes.quote: papers that cannot be replicated are more likely to be cited
vignettes.depicts: A crowd of scholars eagerly copying a tattered, unreliable scroll while a sound intact scroll sits ignored beside it.

plates.title: Two Columns of Cause: Publication and Practice
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page in the same hand as before, aged parchment, black ink line with muted gold, ochre and faded blue wash. The page is split into two tall framed columns side by side, like two cloister aisles, descending in parallel from a shared opening scene at the top: THE ENDLESS PRESS (a press churning scrolls into rafter-high piles), which splits into two ribbon-paths, one into each column. Left column, headed by faint architectural framing suggestive of a publishing-house interior, top to bottom: THE LOCKED DRAWER (a clerk hiding gray scrolls beneath gilded ones on display), THE MISCUT STONES (a mason setting an archway with some wrongly-cut stones), THE SCROLL TREADMILL (a scholar racing a treadmill of scrolls, discarding a sturdy one for a flashier one), THE BLANK-REGION MAP (a traveler holding a map with blank unmarked regions). Right column, headed by a faint laboratory-bench framing, top to bottom: THE CROOKED CROSSROADS (a gambler's hand adjusting dice at a many-pathed table), THE WEAK BOWSTRING (an archer whose bow barely bends, arrows falling short), THE OVERSIZED SACK (a merchant displaying an oversized coin-sack while hiding a smaller true one), THE MISMATCHED TAPESTRY (scholars arguing over a patchwork tapestry of mismatched pieces), THE DIFFERING PLOTS (one seed growing into different plants across several plots). Both columns' final ribbons converge at the bottom of the page into one last shared roundel: THE BENT SCALE (a judge's scale balanced unpredictably on a soft cushion). Keep the two columns visually distinct with a faint inked divider down the center, margins mostly bare but for sparse hairline foliage in the outer corners so the eleven framed scenes remain large and legible. No lettering anywhere on the page except each vignette's title in small capitals beneath its own frame.

vignettes.quote: generation of new data and scientific publications at an unprecedented rate
vignettes.depicts: A press endlessly churning out scrolls faster than any scribe can read them, scrolls piling to the rafters.
vignettes.title: THE ENDLESS PRESS

vignettes.quote: Publication bias—the tendency to publish only positive, significant results—creates the "file drawer effect"
vignettes.depicts: A clerk stuffing plain gray scrolls into a locked drawer beneath a display case of only gilded scrolls.
vignettes.title: THE LOCKED DRAWER

vignettes.quote: 11% of statistical results published in Nature and BMJ in 2001 are "incongruent"
vignettes.depicts: A mason laying inscribed stones into a grand archway, a handful of the stones visibly cut to the wrong measure.
vignettes.title: THE MISCUT STONES

vignettes.quote: incentivizes researchers to prioritize publishable results over validity
vignettes.depicts: A scholar racing on a treadmill of scrolls, tossing aside a sturdy result to grab a flashier one instead.
vignettes.title: THE SCROLL TREADMILL

vignettes.quote: articles often come with insufficient descriptions for other scholars to reproduce the study
vignettes.depicts: A traveler holding a map with whole regions left blank, unable to retrace a described route.
vignettes.title: THE BLANK-REGION MAP

vignettes.quote: Questionable research practices are behaviors that exploit researcher degrees of freedom
vignettes.depicts: A gambler's hand quietly adjusting dice at a table with many open paths painted on the floor before it.
vignettes.title: THE CROOKED CROSSROADS

vignettes.quote: psychology studies have between 33.1% and 36.4% statistical power
vignettes.depicts: A weak archer drawing a bow that barely bends, arrows falling short of a distant target most of the time.
vignettes.title: THE WEAK BOWSTRING

vignettes.quote: Positive effect size bias
vignettes.depicts: A merchant proudly displaying an oversized coin-sack on the scale while a smaller, truer sack sits hidden behind it.
vignettes.title: THE OVERSIZED SACK

vignettes.quote: Meta-analyses have their own methodological problems and disputes
vignettes.depicts: Several scholars arguing over a great stitched-together tapestry made of many smaller mismatched patches.
vignettes.title: THE MISMATCHED TAPESTRY

vignettes.quote: Heterogeneity (variance in research findings due to multiple true effect sizes rather than one)
vignettes.depicts: A single seed sprouting into visibly different plants when grown in several different plots side by side.
vignettes.title: THE DIFFERING PLOTS

vignettes.quote: null hypothesis testing is itself inappropriate, especially in "soft sciences" like social psychology
vignettes.depicts: A judge's scale shown balanced on a soft cushion rather than firm ground, tilting unpredictably.
vignettes.title: THE BENT SCALE
